scope: Two primary-source-verified, software-target API translation/runtime candidates absent from the current catalog and prior staged research: a QEMU macOS guest paravirtual-GPU command-stream bridge, and an experimental source-level Metal-shaped API prototype. Both descriptions restrict compatibility claims to documented interfaces and tests.

projects.title: reims-vgpu
projects.game: macOS guest virtual GPU in QEMU (multi-version software target)
projects.platform: arm64 macOS guests on Apple Silicon macOS hosts (Metal by default; optional Vulkan through MoltenVK), and x86_64 macOS guests on x86_64 Linux/KVM hosts (Vulkan through metal2vulkan)
projects.status: Beta. The README says the implementation has largely stabilized while host- and GPU-driver-dependent differences remain. No GitHub release tags were present on 2026-10-16. The README reports tests for arm64 macOS 13, 14, 15, and 26 guests on an M3 Max, and an x86_64 macOS 26 guest on Linux with an RTX 5080 laptop GPU. Latest default-branch commit checked: c099dd5a4d61107a5527efc64cf1d1ab2f3a9b85 (2026-10-14). These results do not establish support for all guest versions or GPUs.
projects.summary: A QEMU virtual GPU for macOS guests that reuses Apple’s bundled AppleParavirtGPU.kext without installing a guest driver. It replaces the host-side ParavirtualizedGraphics.framework and runs the guest GPU command stream through native Metal on macOS, or through Vulkan on Linux using metal2vulkan. This is a guest paravirtual-GPU command-stream bridge, not a general application-level Metal, Direct3D, or OpenGL compatibility layer; compatibility remains host/GPU dependent.
projects.strategy: Implements the host side of Apple’s macOS paravirtual GPU protocol for QEMU: QEMU apple-gfx devices link a C API to a Rust library, which consumes the guest command stream and submits work to Metal or Vulkan. On Linux, the Vulkan platform uses metal2vulkan; on Apple Silicon, native Metal is the default and an optional Vulkan path uses MoltenVK.
projects.source_available: Public source. Workspace declares GPL-2.0-or-later OR LGPL-3.0-or-later at the recipient’s choice. QEMU and dependencies preserve their own license terms.

projects.title: Metal API emulator experiment
projects.game: Metal-shaped host-side compute and limited render workloads (source-level multi-workload prototype)
projects.platform: Rust source-level Metal-shaped workloads on Linux or Windows through Vulkan, and on macOS through a native Metal provider; Windows guest/QEMU integration is separately experimental and uses a local reims-vgpu adapter
projects.status: Experimental. The README documents a working Rust source-level compute object path and a limited compute/render provider prototype, with native Metal and Vulkan implementations and parity tests. It explicitly says this is not a Metal.framework ABI implementation; arbitrary AIR/MSL, general Metal name resolution, broad render/presentation features, and production reims integration remain incomplete. No GitHub releases were present on 2026-10-16. Latest default-branch commit checked: 226af8c833f9379446dedf744dfa691d760db641 (2026-09-22). Treat its Windows/QEMU census results as maintainer-reported experiments, not general compatibility claims.
projects.summary: An independent Rust prototype that exposes a source-level, Metal-shaped object API and executes supported workloads through a Vulkan provider; a native Metal provider is also used for parity research. The documented path includes buffer compute and a narrow render/present subset. It is not a Metal.framework ABI or binary-compatibility implementation, does not load arbitrary macOS applications, and does not claim full Metal conformance. Its optional integration with reims-vgpu is a local experimental adapter, not an upstream reims architecture.
projects.strategy: Implements Rust Device/Library/Function/pipeline/queue/command-buffer objects and a source-level command contract. The Vulkan provider translates accepted AIR-based workload fixtures through a pinned metal2vulkan revision; a native Metal provider provides a parity rail. Unsupported cases are refused or left outside the implemented subset rather than claimed compatible.
projects.source_available: Public Rust source. Workspace Cargo.toml declares LGPL-3.0-or-later; COPYING and NOTICE identify the incorporated GPL-3 text and separately licensed dependencies/adapters. GitHub detects LGPL-3.0 and GPL-3.0 license files; do not treat the experimental QEMU/reims integration or pinned dependencies as covered by one project-wide term.
projects.subtype: source-level Metal-shaped API prototype with Vulkan/native Metal providers
